title: Lior and the Extraction
premise: Cyrus Winterbourne, a whistle-blower living under four names, works cases no one wants attributed from a network of safe houses. When the current safe house appears on a real estate listing — with photos of the inside, including a shot of Cyrus's own handwriting on a whiteboard — they realize someone has been inside and is deliberately flushing them out. The listing traces back to Meridian Holdings, a shell company tied to an inheritance dispute within the Voss family, whose patriarch once employed Cyrus and whose estate holds proof of a planned infrastructure 'accident' timed to the Geneva summit. As Cyrus races to extract the evidence before the attack, they must decide whether to trust Nadia Voss, the estranged heir who may be bait or ally. In the end, Cyrus stops the attack by exposing it mid-summit, but chooses to surrender their anonymity to testify — trading invisibility for truth.
about_author: Hazel Montrose is a former insurance fraud investigator who spent a decade reconstructing other people's hidden lives before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose careful architectures of secrecy fail in small, human ways.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A routine morning in the Rotterdam safe house establishes Cyrus's tradecraft: rotating identities, burner routines, anonymous casework for lawyers and journalists. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness presented as competence, undercut by a moment where Cyrus almost writes their real name out of habit.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A contact sends a real estate link: the safe house, listed for sale with interior photos — including Cyrus's whiteboard notes about an active case. Panic beneath procedural calm as Cyrus burns the room and plans extraction. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of a life built on invisibility.

chapters.title: Who Took the Photos
chapters.summary: Nadia Voss's POV introduced. Nadia, heir to the Voss estate, reviews the same listing at her family's solicitor's office and realizes the photos were taken months ago — during a period she was told the house was empty. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling into dread that her own inheritance is being weaponized.

chapters.title: Ghost Client
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Tracing the listing to Meridian Holdings, Cyrus finds the shell company's registered address matches a law firm that once paid them anonymously to investigate Voss Industries. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing the case was always about them.

chapters.title: The Old Man's Files
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Sorting her late father's papers, Nadia finds references to a 'Geneva contingency' and a redacted contract with Meridian. Her brother Tomas urges her to sign away her claim and stop asking questions. Emotional beat: loyalty to family pulling against the smell of rot.

chapters.title: Contact Protocol
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Using a dead-drop channel from the old Voss days, Cyrus reaches out to whoever inside the estate leaked the file reference — and gets a reply signed with a phrase only the old man used. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as risk.

chapters.title: Two Strangers, One House
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Cyrus and Nadia agree to meet at the safe house neither can safely enter, each convinced the other set the trap. The meeting is tense, transactional, and ends with both showing a piece of real evidence. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: The Contingency
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Decoding her father's shorthand, Nadia learns the 'accident' targets a summit-bound freight corridor — engineered failure, deniable, insured through Meridian. Emotional beat: grief for her father doubling as horror at what he sanctioned.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Someone leaks one of Cyrus's four identities to a hostile fixer; a near-miss in Antwerp forces a brutal trade-off between protecting a source and staying mobile. Emotional beat: the cost of every name Cyrus has ever borrowed coming due.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Tomas Voss's POV. Charming, cornered, and increasingly desperate, Tomas meets his Meridian handlers and learns he's expendable unless he delivers his sister's signature — or worse. Emotional beat: a weak man discovering how far he'll go not to be the weakest.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Following money rather than people, Cyrus maps Meridian's insurance positions and proves the 'accident' is a payout scheme requiring the summit timeline. Emotional beat: cold clarity — motive found, clock started.

chapters.title: Safe House Rules
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hiding together in a secondary bolt-hole, Cyrus and Nadia build the plan and, reluctantly, trust. Nadia challenges why Cyrus hides; Cyrus deflects, then doesn't. Emotional beat: intimacy as vulnerability neither can afford but both choose.

chapters.title: The Insider
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia identifies the estate insider who photographed the house: her father's longtime caretaker, coerced years ago via a debt Meridian owns. Confronting him yields the access codes to the estate vault. Emotional beat: compassion for a broken man, and fury at what coercion does.

chapters.title: Vault
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Night entry into the Voss estate vault while Tomas's security sweeps the grounds. Cyrus retrieves the contingency file — full schematics, timing, and a list of names paid to look away. Emotional beat: triumph immediately shadowed by alarms and the realization they were expected.

chapters.title: Framed
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas tips off authorities that 'a whistle-blower' stole from the estate, making Cyrus the perfect scapegoat if anything goes wrong in Geneva. Emotional beat: self-justification wearing the mask of duty.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The escape route is compromised; a chase through the estate's orchards ends with Nadia taking a bullet meant for Cyrus. Emotional beat: guilt detonating — Cyrus's invisibility has made everyone around them a target.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV, hospital-bound. Wounded and furious, Nadia confronts Cyrus's instinct to vanish alone and forces the question: is disappearing loyalty to anyone, or just fear with better discipline? Emotional beat: the theme stated as accusation.

chapters.title: The Summit Opens
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Delegates arrive in Geneva; Meridian's engineers make final adjustments to the corridor's signaling systems under cover of maintenance contracts. Tomas receives his final instructions. Emotional beat: dread tightening like a ratchet.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Minutes
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. With the file authenticated by a summit journalist, Cyrus has minutes to convince security services that the 'maintenance window' is the attack — without revealing how they know, which would burn them. Emotional beat: the ultimate test of whether truth can outrun anonymity.

chapters.title: The Accident That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. The corridor failsafe is tripped early; the derailment is prevented as Cyrus goes public on a live feed, naming Meridian, the ledger, and themselves. Tomas breaks and confesses on camera to save himself. Emotional beat: exposure as both victory and wound.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In the aftermath, prosecutors offer Cyrus continued anonymity in exchange for quiet cooperation. Cyrus declines and requests formal witness status instead. Emotional beat: choosing a name — the first one honestly held in years.

chapters.title: One Name
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating Cyrus and Nadia. Months later, Cyrus testifies under their own name while Nadia rebuilds the estate as a foundation for coerced insiders like the caretaker. They meet once more at the old safe house — now genuinely for sale. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited; the door finally open.
